detail.abstract: I study how information sharing creates value in global audit networks by examining restrictions on cross-border transfers of client data. Using a global sample of such restrictions, I find that top-10 firms shift labor to affected affiliates, raising audit fees without detectably affecting audit timeliness or restatements. Within affected countries, staffing rises most in offices serving clients that are more data-intensive and organizationally integrated across borders, consistent with impaired cross-border coordination. Despite these frictions, top-10 affiliates retain more audit work within network and gain local market share, suggesting that the increased value of trusted affiliates operating under common quality controls more than offsets networks' diminished ability to coordinate across borders. Overall, the evidence highlights two information channels that help global audit networks allocate labor efficiently: sharing client data enables networks to coordinate audit work across affiliates, whereas confidence in affiliate work quality allows them to delegate work locally when those data cannot be shared.

title: International Market Entry Challenges Facing SMEs in the GCC

detail.title: International Market Entry Challenges Facing SMEs in the GCC

detail.abstract:
This project aims to address the problem encountered by SMEs in the GCC region while trying to enter the international market. The fundamental problem in this scenario is that even if there are growth opportunities in the international arena, this does not necessarily mean that it will result in successful market entry. There could be small firms with promising goods or services that lack the necessary organizational resources, foreign market knowledge and organizational capability together with external relations required for operation in the new foreign environment.

The research approach used in this project is desk based secondary research guided by pragmatism. The data was gathered from research papers, systematic review papers and reliable institutions with more preference towards studies done in the GCC and the Middle Eastern regions if any. The study is divided into three major inter-related themes which are organizational resources and capabilities, foreign market knowledge, and business networks and strategic relations.

Results show that the process of internationalization should not be considered as an issue of financing alone. The literature from Qatar demonstrates that export success is linked to such factors as networking abilities, supply chain management, digitalization, product diversification and market intelligence (Elsharnouby et al., 2024). Other academic studies show that market intelligence can be achieved through experience, information and business connections, while networks can offer SMEs knowledge and resources that cannot be gained otherwise (Costa, Soares and de Sousa, 2016; Puthusserry et al., 2020).

As a result of this research, the three perspectives appear to be most effective when used together. Uppsala perspective explains the process of learning and uncertainty, RBV perspective provides explanation for differences in internal capabilities, while the network theory explains access to external knowledge and resources. Based on these results, the report offers a number of recommendations such as formal market-readiness assessment, market intelligence procedure, network formation, proper entry mode and internal capability building.

title: Synthetic Rationality: The Behavioral Macroeconomics of Cognitive Offloading to Generative AI

detail.title: Synthetic Rationality: The Behavioral Macroeconomics of Cognitive Offloading to Generative AI

detail.abstract: Generative AI supplies the first synthetic counterpart to System 2: an external deliberative surrogate available at near-zero cost and latency. This paper introduces the Surrogate System 2 as an extension of Kahneman's dual-process architecture and argues that habitual offloading substitutes for, rather than augments, biological deliberation. Four propositions formalize the claim: (P1) deliberation is now externalizable at near-zero private cost; (P2) externalization severs the metacognitive cues, disfluency and the demand to explain, that recruit System 2; (P3) deliberative capacity is a depreciating stock with asymmetric restoration costs, not an optimizable flow; and (P4) mode of engagement, set by interface defaults, determines whether the surrogate replaces reasoning or exercises it. Read against the leading formal treatment (Acemoglu, Kong, and Ozdaglar, 2026), the stock-flow distinction overturns the model's Pigouvian and information-design remedies, which fail on behavioral, fiscal, measurement, and geopolitical grounds. The resulting condition, Synthetic Rationality, is analyzed through Minsky, Hayek, and Schumpeter as a structural feature of current institutional configurations rather than a parameter failure. Its manifestations run from the collapse of the expert premium and Minskyan cognitive fragility to a cognitive balance of payments deficit in the Global South and an illusion of explanatory depth manufactured at scale. The same technology then bifurcates outcomes by mode of engagement: a majority whose consumption of fluent output depreciates deliberative capacity, and an elite whose interrogation of the models still recruits System 2. Knowledge collapse is the outcome of these arrangements, as opposed to a precision parameter set too low.

title: The Judgment Bottleneck: Why the Same AI Agent Speeds up Novices and Slows Down Experts

detail.title: The Judgment Bottleneck: Why the Same AI Agent Speeds up Novices and Slows Down Experts

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.

detail.abstract:
Agentic AI has driven the marginal cost of producing a candidate artifact — a patch, a draft, a plan — toward zero. Delivered output has not risen by the same factor, and randomized trials disagree on the sign: recruited developers on a greenfield task were 56 percent faster; experienced developers on repositories they had maintained for years were 19 percent slower. This paper gives a model in which both are expected and derives the quantity that separates them.

The human collaborator has a bounded daily budget of judgment time, and verification — establishing that an artifact is what it appears to be — is what consumes it. Delegation collapses generation time but leaves verification standing, and often larger, because the verifier must reconstruct context an author would have held. Delegation therefore raises delivered output per human-hour if and only if the generation time it saves, net of specification and — when the human does not wait — switching, exceeds this verification penalty. Decomposing the penalty into a part that falls with task experience and a part that does not yields, under stated sign conditions, a unique experience level above which delegation lowers output — the sign pattern the trials show, though the durations that would test it have not yet been read this way.

A second result shows that the efficient verification depth does not rise as the prior on correctness rises and does not fall as the liability for error rises; because budget pressure also lowers depth, appropriate reliance and rubber-stamping produce identical acceptance rates. Mapping depth onto signal-detection sensitivity, criterion, and time-on-artifact gives the design that separates them, and the remedies differ: capacity for a fall in sensitivity, incentives for a shift in criterion. The paper also gives a partition of rationing responses to judgment scarcity and shows that their joint appearance in 2026 engineering telemetry is implied by any capacity constraint and does not by itself confirm a cognitive account. Seven hypotheses, five designs, and implications for tool design, review capacity, and the EU AI Act's human-oversight provisions follow.

detail.abstract: Organizations produce current decisions and future decision makers through the same work. We introduce the diagnostic record as a new organizational output: the information current work leaves about the criterion behind a decision. This yields a theory of how AI separates execution from the reproduction of judgment. Because correct actions need not reveal that criterion, greater value from AI-originated decisions can expand scale while reducing developmental opportunities and successful succession. In multidimensional problems, verified AI information can replace some diagnostic experiences but not others. AI can therefore make expertise easier to deploy while making independent decision makers harder to produce.

detail.abstract: Purpose. Every founder of a social enterprise is eventually asked why the organisation is not simply a company or a charity. The standard answers-the double bottom line, earned income, legitimacy, policy access, hybrid innovation-are true of most social enterprises and constitutive of none. This paper identifies a class of social enterprise for which the form is not a choice but a structural necessity, and supplies a diagnostic by which any organisation can determine whether it belongs to that class. Approach. Conceptual and comparative-institutional, grounded in a readout-relative epistemology: every record an institution holds about a person is a bounded readout of that person's state, never the state itself, and distinctions collapsed by an early readout cannot be recovered by later readers. From this the paper defines positional governance-the capacity of an actor that holds a transaction to bind itself, credibly and enforceably, against the completion incentive of that same transaction-and the position-holding enterprise, whose product is a condition on a transaction that would otherwise proceed unconditioned. A counterfactual removal test locates the mechanism; nine requirements are derived and tested against five institutional archetypes; four mechanisms of fit are specified. A Thai nikah (Islamic marriage) service that became a registered social enterprise in 2024 illustrates each step; applications in labour recruitment and consumer credit show the class is not confined to one sector. The paper integrates, as one argument, three previously separate strands: a theory of positional governance, a dual-cost account of what holding the position costs, and a survival model of the capital that can hold it-and closes with a toolkit through which any organisation can run the diagnostic on itself. Methodologically it is conceptual and comparative-institutional with a reflexive practitioner-inquiry component: practice experience generates the problem and the propositions; it does not by itself establish prevalence. Findings. Within the arrangements examined, only the registered social enterprise holds the transaction position while being bound to an objective other than completion; for the position-holding class the form is constitutive, for the revenue-for-mission and mission-in-product classes it is convenient. A three-question Position Test distinguishes the classes; seven conditions define binding sufficiency, the seventh being capital admissibility. Mission drift for the class is redefined as the degeneration of a condition-gate into one that cannot fail, and is measurable by invocation rates and revenue forgone; a stop rule that is never invoked is shown to be a non-readout rather than evidence of safety. A dual-cost account-hard capital, and a soft layer decomposed into binding costs and condition costs-yields a state-support corollary: money-only support misprices the class; support should also fund audit and certification infrastructure and recognise revenue forgone as qualifying performance. Originality. Two systematic prior-art reviews-across social-enterprise typology, gatekeeper theory, legalform-as-commitment, safeguarding evaluation, mission-drift measurement, steward-ownership, legitimacy theory, certification economics, and comparative promotion policy-find the paper's four claims partially anticipated in their motivations and components and not found in their formulations within the stated search scope. The paper is positioned as a self-conscription complement to gatekeeper theory and a positional complement to hybrid-organisation theory. Limits of the form-no authority, depth without coverage, borrowed legitimacy, rebinding without removal-and falsification conditions are stated with equal weight.

title: Consequences at the Gate: Which Tasks Appear in Public Data on Generative AI Use?

detail.title: Consequences at the Gate: Which Tasks Appear in Public Data on Generative AI Use?

detail.abstract:
Measures of AI task exposure describe where generative AI may apply, but not necessarily which tasks appear in public tables based on provider-classified interactions. We ask whether representation varies with the consequences of errors not readily caught before taking effect. We link four January and March 2026 Anthropic Economic Index tables for Claude.ai and Anthropic's first-party API to O*NET task descriptions and construct an outcome-blind, O*NET-informed five-point consequence score. A description is represented if any table reports a positive share. The sample contains 18,163 descriptions uniquely linked to 775 occupations in the AEI task map. Within occupations, representation is approximately flat at scores one through three and lower at scores four and five. A linear specification estimates an average gradient of -2.66 percentage points per score point, relative to a 21.4 percent mean. Each table-specific coefficient is negative; separate Qwen3.8-27B ratings yield a similar gradient, and the gradient remains negative when representation is defined using only task-use cells classified as work. Occupation means of the primary task score correlate with the official O*NET Consequence of Error measure (r = 0.68), although the paper has no human ratings of the same descriptions. In a complete-measure comparison, the consequence coefficient remains negative when five related task dimensions and task controls enter jointly; none of the five comparison measures is negative. Because representation combines interaction patterns, provider classification, and reporting filters, the estimates describe public-table representation rather than workplace adoption or causal effects. The available GPT-4 task-exposure measure does not eliminate the negative within-occupation association.
AI-use disclosure. GPT-5 mini and Qwen3.8-27B were used to produce the task-level ratings described in the paper. Generative AI was also used for limited code review and language-editing assistance; all substantive claims, empirical decisions, and final text were reviewed and approved by the author.

detail.abstract: This article comprehensively evaluates virtual reality environments (VREs) as a setting for experiments in marketing research. The key notion is that VREs can create a sensation of telepresence, which can advance certain experimental validities, providing stronger experimental results. Using a process model of conducting experiments, the article then compares experimentation in VREs to online, laboratory, and field experiments, as well as explores existing methods and technologies commonly used within marketing research. The article finally illustrates the benefits of experimentation in VREs along the customer journey. The key contribution of this article is to extend the current knowledge of marketing researchers on experimentation in VREs with the goal of popularizing conducting research in this unique setting.

detail.abstract: We model artificial intelligence (AI) as a distinct capital input in a nested CES aggregate production function that extends work done by Krusell et al. (2000) and embed it in a dynamic general equilibrium economy. By bringing the model to the data, we estimate the degree to which AI either substitutes for or complements the other production inputs at the aggregate level. We find that AI is complementary to the high-skill–equipment composite and that the AI weight in production remains small. We then use the model to study how this complementarity shapes the macroeconomic and distributional effects of AI capital accumulation. The estimated model implies different effects of alternative AI shocks. A rise in the AI usage share is contractionary as it increases reliance on a scarce complementary input. A fall in AI prices is expansionary due to the lower cost of accumulating AI capital. A tax on AI capital income raises limited revenue while the AI capital stock remains small, but can finance welfare-improving transfers as the AI price falls. A large-scale universal basic income (UBI) funded jointly by a consumption tax slows AI investment with welfare gains for low-skill workers at the expense of losses for high-skill workers and entrepreneurs. On the measurement side, we construct a quality-adjusted AI price index from hedonic regressions and build a corresponding AI capital stock.

title: What Makes Systemic Banks Different: Structural Characteristics and their Implications for Stakeholder Risk Preferences and Excessive Risk Appetite

detail.title: What Makes Systemic Banks Different: Structural Characteristics and their Implications for Stakeholder Risk Preferences and Excessive Risk Appetite

detail.abstract:
Corporate governance scholarship, and the corporate law that reflects it, developed around the non-financial firm. Its core proposition is that shareholders, as residual claimants with comparatively homogeneous interests, are the constituency whose interests management should serve. It is presumed that when management maximises the residual, the value of every other claim against the firm will also be maximised. This paper asks whether the proposition survives transposition to the operating environment of systemically important banks, and concludes that it does not.

The paper identifies nine structural characteristics that distinguish banking from most other industries: 1) the composition of the stakeholder base, 2) leverage, 3) liquidity mismatch, 4) rapid asset substitution, 5) balance sheet opaqueness, 6) negative externalities, 7) deposit insurance, 8) implicit too-big-to-fail guarantees, and 9) the extent and intrusiveness of regulation. The paper traces the effect of each characteristic on the incentives of the bank's constituencies. It then develops a taxonomy of stakeholder risk preferences, separating risk-prone, risk-neutral and risk-averse groups, and cross-references those preferences against each group's capacity to influence the risk actually taken within the firm.

The central finding is a structural misalignment between risk preference and power. The constituencies with the strongest appetite for risk (shareholders, directors and senior management) are largely those best placed to determine the institution's risk profile, while the risk-neutral and risk-averse constituencies (e.g. creditors and the general public) have relatively little influence over the institution’s risk-taking. Supervisors are the exception: their preferences are aligned with the public's and their instruments to influence risk-taking are powerful, but they act without capital at risk and are exposed to capture.

The paper argues that without proper regulatory intervention, this incentive misalignment between stakeholder groups leads to excessive risk taking from the perspective of the broader society, particularly because the conventional notion of “good” corporate governance, which aims to align the interests of owners and managers, intensifies rather than mitigates the problem.

detail.abstract: Policy benchmarks from upper-tier governments can influence local policies without legal restrictions or financial incentives. This paper examines how local governments respond to policy benchmarks set by upper-tier governments, focusing on a reform of Japan's National Health Insurance. The reform introduced benchmarks for each municipality's insurance premiums, making premiums more salient and influencing premium-setting. We find that municipalities whose premiums initially exceeded the benchmark reduced premiums by an amount equivalent to about 5 percent of the pre-reform mean, with the effect growing over time. We also find larger premium-reduction effects among municipalities with a larger initial gap between the benchmark and the premium, as well as among those with greater fiscal capacity. These findings are robust across a series of robustness checks. The findings suggest that policy benchmarks can affect local policy choices at relatively low cost. We also find that municipalities partly offset the premium reduction through higher discretionary general-account transfers, while finding little evidence of expenditure-side or balance-sheet adjustments.

detail.abstract: Regulators, investors, and civil society increasingly demand credible climate risk disclosure and ESG sustainability reporting, yet manual audit review cannot keep pace with the volume of corporate disclosures, and premature or overconfident public greenwashing accusations carry genuine reputational and legal risk for both the accusing party and the accused firm. Building on a study applying data science techniques to predictive analytics in financial services, this study generalizes that predictive-analytics paradigm into an AI-augmented ESG/climate disclosure risk-screening architecture with an explicit, trustcalibrated auditor-escalation layer. Three formal research questions are addressed: whether AI-based multi-signal screening significantly outperforms traditional threshold-based audit review (RQ1), whether a confidence-gated escalation policy significantly reduces the missed-greenwashing rate relative to unconditional AI screening (RQ2), and what the quantified, statistically grounded false-accusation cost of that policy is (RQ3). Using a literature-informed synthetic dataset of 12,000 firm-level disclosure records spanning four greenwashing-risk levels, three configurations, a traditional rule-based audit baseline, an AI-only predictive screening model, and an AI model with confidence-gated escalation to human auditor review were evaluated on an illustrative held-out split and, to test the study's hypotheses rigorously, across 30 independently resampled train/test trials with paired statistical testing and a fixed escalation threshold. The AI-only configuration was dramatically and significantly more accurate than the traditional rule-based baseline across all 30 trials (mean 89.4% versus 51.3%, paired t-test p < .0001, Cohen's d = 38.4), confirming H1. The escalation configuration showed a statistically significant, though practically small, reduction in missed-greenwashing rate relative to AI-only (mean difference 0.08 percentage points, p < .0001, Cohen's d = 0.85), confirming H2 while illustrating that a highly consistent effect across trials can be statistically significant without being large in absolute terms. The escalation configuration's falseaccusation rate was significantly higher than AI-only's (mean increase 2.50 percentage points, p < .0001, Cohen's d = 4.97), confirming H3 and quantifying the disclosed reputational-risk cost of the escalation policy. The study contributes a generalized, reusable architecture for AI-augmented, trust-calibrated ESG/climate disclosure risk screening, a reproducible sensitivity-sweep and statistical-validation methodology, and transparent, hypothesis-tested empirical evidence characterizing the missedgreenwashing/false-accusation trade-off central to responsible AI-augmented sustainability-disclosure oversight. Limitations, implications, and directions for future research are discussed.

detail.abstract: International market entry involves not only which markets to serve but also when to enter them, yet the timing implications of cross-national distance remain poorly understood. This paper examines how economic and geographic distance shape the timing of foreign market entry and how these effects differ between multinationals from developed and emerging economies. We theorize that both distance dimensions entail offsetting costs and benefits whose relative importance shifts with distance: low distance facilitates efficiency and knowledge transfer, moderate distance amplifies adaptation costs without commensurate advantages, and high distance can create arbitrage opportunities, competitive insulation, and access to strategic assets. Using a sample of 327 entries by 36 international telecom operators into 112 mobile broadband markets worldwide, results show significant inverted U-shaped effects of both economic and geographic distance on entry timing. The curvature is stronger for companies from developed economies compared to entrants from emerging economies. The study extends nonlinear distance research to entry timing, identifies firm origin as a boundary condition for distance-timing effects, and introduces a methodological template for more credible estimation of distance effects. Managerially, the findings challenge the view that distant markets should always be entered later, indicating instead that both very proximate and very distant markets may warrant early entry, whereas intermediate-distance markets pose the greatest timing challenges.

title: FLCG: Fusing Fine-grained Local Features and Contextual Global Features Graph Learning for Multimodal Recommendation

detail.title: FLCG: Fusing Fine-grained Local Features and Contextual Global Features Graph Learning for Multimodal Recommendation
detail.abstract: Multimodal recommendation systems enhance recommendation accuracy by integrating user interaction behaviors with item-side multimodal information (e.g., visual and textual features). However, existing works still face two critical challenges: (1) Coarse-grained ID representation, where traditional holistic vector representations fail to disentangle users' complex latent intents; and (2) Insufficient utilization of global information, as local graph convolution aggregation struggles to capture long-range structural dependencies and global semantic context. To address the above issues, this paper proposes a graph learning method for multimodal recommendation that fuses fine-grained local features and contextual global features (FLCG). FLCG uniformly models user preferences from two complementary perspectives, local and global. From the local perspective, we design an ID Intent Disentanglement Module and a Local Modal Fusion Module. The former accurately captures micro-level user interests by decomposing ID embeddings into fine-grained intent chunks, while the latter achieves feature alignment of multimodal information within the local neighborhood. From the global perspective, we introduce a Hypergraph Attention Aggregation Module and a Modal Prototype Learning Module, which effectively capture high-order global dependencies often missed by traditional methods, from the aspects of full-graph topology and cross-modal semantic commonality, respectively. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that FLCG outperforms existing state-of-the-art baselines across various key metrics. These results demonstrate the practical potential of FLCG to support more accurate personalized recommendation and item discovery in real-world platforms, particularly under sparse user–item interaction scenarios.  Code is available at https://github.com/GNNETlab/FLCG.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing how organizations in the United States recruit, select, develop, manage and retain employees in the HRM space. Recruitment and Selection, Workforce Analytics, Performance Management, Learning, Development and Engagement, Strategic Workforce Planning are increasingly becoming areas where AI technologies are being used in recruitment. While AI in HRM presents many opportunities to optimize organizational efficiency and boost the productivity of the workforce, it also has many challenges associated with it, such as algorithmic bias, employee privacy, AI transparency, human autonomy, ethical decision making, and organizational readiness. In this research, the authors investigate how AI-powered HRM can boost employee productivity and boost the company's competitiveness in the United States. This study uses a systematic and integrative literature review methodology, to provide a synthesis of the evidence from peer-reviewed academic research and pertinent scholarly literature related to the adoption of AI and the impact on HRM practices and organisational outcomes. The results show that AI-driven HRM can help enhance the productivity of the workforce by speeding up decision-making, automating repetitive admin tasks, helping to tailor employee growth, predictive workforce analysis, and talent allocation, among other ways. In addition, AI can help organizations become more competitive by better strategically planning their workforce, recruiting talent, improving innovation, and being more agile. The benefits are however, dependent to a large extent, on good implementation, good human oversight, good quality data, trust of employees and strong ethical oversight. The study also finds that AI should be used as a tool to supplement, not replace, HR professionals in their decision making process. To optimize productivity, ensure the safety of employees and maintain the competitiveness of organizations in the changing landscape of the U.S. workplace, a balanced human-AI approach is therefore essential (Malik et al., 2023; Basu et al., 2023; Tambe et al., 2019; Budhwar et al., 2023).

detail.abstract: This paper studies whether disagreement inside the Federal Open Market Committee predicts how much markets update when the public statement arrives. It classifies policy-round remarks from internal transcripts and constructs a smoothed stance for every participant. Separately, it extracts numerical rate actions from 200 Bluebook and Tealbook policy menus covering 1995 to 2019. Controlling for public information, projection dates, and Chair-period fixed effects, both an increase in disagreement and an increase in option-menu dispersion predict significantly larger absolute Gürkaynak-Sack-Swanson target surprises. These relationships hold only for short-maturity components, not for the path factor or changes in longer-term yields. However, the topic-modelling results show that greater emphasis on statement language and public communication is associated with smaller absolute monetary policy surprises. Private disagreement creates the potential for a large public surprise, but greater attention to statement language and public communication may absorb part of that potential shock before the announcement.

detail.abstract: We examine how individual investors weigh personal experience against public information in their trading decisions. Using approximately 61,000 retail foreign exchange traders and over 60 million directional trades, we estimate the relative weight on each signal with a discrete choice model. On average the weight on personal experience is 0.56: traders rely on the two signals about equally, with a small but reliable tilt toward their own experience. This average hides systematic variation that follows a principle established in neuroscience and economics-investors place more weight on whichever signal they perceive as more reliable. The weight on personal experience rises when a trader's own record becomes the more reliable signal: when they trade more intensely and build a denser recent history, and for sterling pairs during the Brexit campaign and the October 2016 flash crash, when political news and an anomalous price move made recent prices less reliable. It falls when public information becomes the more reliable signal: around scheduled central-bank announcements, when new information moves prices, and as traders gain experience and become more confident in interpreting price dynamics. Benchmarked against each signal's power to predict the direction of price changes, traders respond to each signal with the correct sign but overweight public information and underweight personal experience. These findings indicate that the process through which investors learn from public information is dynamic: it depends on how reliable they perceive public information to be relative to their personal experience.

detail.abstract: Firm characteristics are commonly represented as fixed vectors, even though evidence about firms' operations arrives as heterogeneous collections of articles and reports. We study how distances between distributions of firm characteristics restrict systematic covariance. For given latent exposure laws, quadratic Wasserstein geometry yields sharp covariance endpoints over admissible couplings. Under a common randomized bi-Lipschitz characteristic-to-exposure map, bounded risk-coordinate slack, and a maintained return-covariance bridge, characteristic-side distance yields a conditional interval for the covariance ceiling. Greater separation then leaves less scope for aligned systematic exposures when these assumptions are tight, while a nonnegative transportexcess term records the gap between realized and maximum-covariance arrangements. The resulting envelope is scenario analysis rather than an expected-return, no-arbitrage, or identified structural model. Empirically, we proxy characteristic distributions with encoder-only language-model embeddings of financial news articles, disclosures, and analyst reports for Nasdaq firms over 2018-2022. In a dyadic regression with symmetric firm effects, greater pairwise article-embedding W 2 distance is associated with weaker return co-movement: the coefficient is 1.920, with 95% interval [1.412, 2.468]. The estimate retains the same sign when returns are measured in a later window, although the feature construction is not point-in-time and the evidence remains reduced form.

detail.abstract: Modern enterprise networks suffer from vulnerability fatigue caused by high-volume automated port and service scans. Existing vulnerability assessment systems frequently generate uncontextualized lists of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) without providing actionable insight into execution paths or threat actor Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs). In this paper, we present PwnTrace, an open-source, modular security assessment framework that integrates active service fingerprinting, dynamic NVD vulnerability correlation, heuristic MITRE ATT&CK mapping, and automated attack-path synthesis. We evaluate PwnTrace within an isolated testbed (Metasploitable 2) targeting 18 active services across 50 CVE candidates. PwnTrace successfully completes discovery, correlation, TTP mapping, and path generation in approximately 10.4 seconds, accurately prioritizing critical entry vectors.

detail.abstract: This paper develops and estimates a structural model linking population agglomeration, spatial centrality, salary-cap constraints, and NBA team efficiency. Using team-season data from 2000–2024, fixed-effects models show a U-shaped relationship between metropolitan population and wins per payroll dollar, consistent with a Mid-Market Inefficiency Trough (MMIT). The paper includes an Urban Centrality Index (UCI), measured as arena distance from the metropolitan central business district, to distinguish market scale from within-market spatial position. UCI also enters nonlinearly, producing a spatial efficiency trough. Salary-cap expansion is associated with lower payroll efficiency in the league's fixed-win environment. Ordered probit estimates provide corroborating postseason evidence: payroll relative to the salary cap is positively associated with advancement, population retains a nonlinear association with RoundWins, and the return to payroll declines with arena-CBD distance. Together, the findings support a multilevel agglomeration-congestion framework in which metropolitan scale shapes competitive capacity and spatial centrality affects payroll efficiency and conditions postseason payroll returns.

detail.abstract: \begin{abstract}\textbf{Background:} Tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus (ToLCNDV) is an emerging threat to global cucurbit production, with transmission strongly influenced by climatic conditions and farmer management decisions. However, existing mathematical models rarely integrate environmental forcing, vector--host epidemiology, and adaptive farmer behavior within a unified framework. This study develops a coupled climate--epidemiological--socio-economic model to investigate how these interacting mechanisms shape ToLCNDV transmission and control. \textbf{Main findings:} The epidemiological component employs an SEIR structure for cucurbit plants and an SI structure for the whitefly vector. Temperature and relative humidity are incorporated explicitly through nonlinear response functions governing vector recruitment, transmission efficiency, mortality, and disease progression. Farmer adaptation is represented by an evolutionary game-theoretic replicator equation, with adoption of climate-smart practices enhancing rogueing and vector-control rates. We derive a climate- and behavior-dependent basic reproduction number, $\mathcal{R}_0(T_0, H_0, x_a^*)$, and establish positivity, boundedness, and well-posedness of the model. A Lyapunov analysis proves global asymptotic stability of the disease-free equilibrium for $\mathcal{R}_0 < 1$, while bifurcation analysis demonstrates a forward transcritical bifurcation at $\mathcal{R}_0 = 1$ and excludes backward bifurcation. PRCC analysis identifies farmer adoption as the strongest negative driver of $\mathcal{R}_0$. Seasonal simulations reveal climate-driven epidemic waves and a dynamic feedback whereby disease pressure increases farmer adoption, subsequently reducing epidemic peaks. \textbf{Conclusions:} The results demonstrate that climate-smart interventions can generate reinforcing socio-epidemiological feedbacks that enhance disease suppression. Policies that reduce the economic barriers to adoption may therefore promote sustained, community-driven control of ToLCNDV under climatic variability.\end{abstract}

detail.title: Commuting-network change between 2017 and 2021: A distance-aware graph attention and explainable-learning framework for Belgium
detail.abstract: Changes in work practices and mobility conditions during the COVID-19 period coincided with substantial interest in how commuting networks may have reorganized. This study compares Belgian commuting flows observed in 2017 and 2021 and develops a distance-aware graph attention network (DAGAT) combined with an XGBoost flow decoder. The analysis uses harmonized origin–destination records for 581 zones, population, 26 land-use attributes, geographic contiguity, and inter-zonal distance. After excluding intrazonal movements and origin–destination flows below five commuters, the analytical samples contain 18,006 records in 2017 and 17,958 in 2021, representing approximately 70% of surveyed commuters. Network indicators show small declines in mean degree (62.24 to 61.92), mean strength (2,897.19 to 2,865.82), clustering (0.0066 to 0.0058), and Moran’s I (0.0049 to 0.0048). In the archived 60/20/20 split, DAGAT–XGBoost achieved RMSE = 55.393, CPC = 0.757, and R2 = 0.760, outperforming gravity, radiation, and reference graph-learning specifications. Gradient saliency suggests that population and banking/office land use remained prominent predictors, while the relative ranking of several open-space, road, water, and undeveloped-land attributes was higher in 2021. These results describe temporal associations rather than pandemic effects: only two cross-sections are observed, and uncertainty estimates and repeated spatial validation were not available. The findings support policy use of graph-based prediction for network monitoring while cautioning against interpreting model saliency as causal evidence for land-use intervention.

detail.abstract: Portfolio risk assessment ordinarily relies on reliable estimates of cross-asset return covariances, which are difficult to obtain in short, high-dimensional panels. We show that firm-level distribution-valued characteristics can instead provide one-sided certificates of portfolio risk. Under maintained links from characteristics to systematic exposures and from exposures to returns, multi-firm Wasserstein-2 dispersion yields a sharp upper bound on systematic portfolio variance and a corresponding bound for standardized returns. A weighted pairwise relaxation produces an objective that is convex under a checkable condition and requires marginal volatility scales but no cross-asset return covariances. With zero firm-specific slack, the common-map scale changes the certified variance reduction but not the normalized allocation, which depends only on observed information geometry. In a 52-firm panel from 2018-2022, an allocation constructed from Qwen3-Embedding-8B news representations lies between the 0.69th and 1.33rd in-sample variance percentiles across four prespecified capped portfolio populations; equal risk weighting lies between the 21.1st and 28.6th percentiles. The lower in-sample variance ranking relative to equal risk also appears across the reported frozen language-model representations. The framework therefore converts distribution-valued firm information into a coherent risk bound and an implementable allocation rule constructed without cross-asset return covariances.

detail.abstract: In 2024, I conducted a survey of 143 professional tax return preparers to seek information about whether and how they use IRS publications " a source of informal IRS guidance. Survey respondents do make use of IRS publications, typically alongside other sources. In some cases, IRS informal guidance contains statements that are susceptible to interpretations that are, at least arguably, inconsistent with formal legal sources. In a previous study, I presented examples of such statements to non-experts, and many of the non-experts interpreted the statements in ways that were, indeed, potentially inconsistent with formal legal guidance. Plausibly, tax return preparers are less likely to interpret the statements this way. In the current study, I presented several of the same scenarios and IRS publication language to tax return preparers. In one of the scenarios, tax law provides a clear answer. When presented with this scenario and after reading the applicable IRS publication language, 76.9% of the return preparers selected the correct tax treatment, compared to 57% of the non-experts in the previous study. This result aligns with previous studies finding that, when tax law is clear, professional preparers tend to steer taxpayers toward reporting the correct tax treatment. Nevertheless, it is noteworthy that even some of the return preparers did not select the correct treatment. Meanwhile, previous studies tend to show that, when tax law is governed by vague standards, professional tax return preparers steer taxpayers towards claiming taxpayer-favorable positions. In two of the scenarios in this survey, the correct tax treatment is unclear. IRS publications, however, describe applicable law as clearly disallowing a deduction. When asked whether they think a hypothetical client is allowed to claim a deduction after considering the information in the IRS publication, most of the professional tax return preparers (83% in one scenario and 75.5% in another) indicated that they did not think the client was allowed to claim a deduction. These numbers are comparable to non-experts (the corresponding figures were 77% and 78%). These results offer some tentative support for the possibility that, when they present standard-based questions of tax law as, instead, governed by clear taxpayer-unfavorable rules, IRS publications may dampen the tendency of professional tax return preparers to recommend pro-taxpayer positions in response to uncertainty.

detail.abstract:
Background: Multimorbidity is an increasing challenge in the Americas, yet evidence from Latin America remains limited, and health systems largely retain single-disease approaches. We examined regional multimorbidity patterns in Colombia using national administrative health data. 

Methods: We conducted a network analysis using anonymized data from the Colombian Ministry of Health and Social Protection (2016–2019). Sixteen chronic conditions were identified from ICD-10 codes, procedures, and medication records according to the Charlson Comorbidity Index. We estimated regional prevalence and identified over-represented disease pairs relative to Bogotá DC using Fisher’s exact tests (P ≤ 0.001), followed by network analysis of significant pairs. The study followed STROBE guidelines. 

Findings:  We analyzed 15,192,282 adults across Bogotá D.C. (4,438,346), Central (4,251,215), Eastern (2,254,458), Pacific (2,169,590), and Atlantic (2,078,673) regions. Diabetes mellitus was the most prevalent condition across all regions. Patterns of over-represented disease pairs varied geographically. Compared with Bogotá D.C., liver disease with retinopathy was over-represented in Central and Eastern regions, liver disease with neuropathy in Atlantic, and diabetes mellitus with paraplegia–hemiplegia in Pacific.​ 

Interpretation: Regional variation in multimorbidity suggests that uniform national programs might not adequately reflect local needs. Screening, referral, and integrated-care pathways could be adapted to regionally over-represented condition combinations. Combining administrative health data with network methods offers a scalable approach for identifying geographically distinct multimorbidity patterns and informing integrated care across Latin America and the Caribbean.

detail.abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive examination of the Energy Charter Treaty (ECT), tracing its historical foundations, analysing its present-day application, and evaluating the prospects for its future reform or abandonment. It begins by situating the ECT in its post-Cold War geopolitical context, explaining how the Treaty was designed to foster cross-border energy cooperation and attract foreign investment into transitional economies. The analysis then turns to the Treaty’s structure, with particular emphasis on its investor–State dispute settlement (ISDS) mechanism and substantive investment protections, such as fair and equitable treatment and protection against expropriation. The chapter critically assesses how these provisions have been interpreted in arbitral practice, drawing on Italy’s extensive experience as a respondent State in ECT-based disputes concerning renewable and fossil fuel investments. Special attention is given to intra-EU jurisdictional objections, the treaty’s conflict clause, and the enduring relevance of the so-called sunset clause. The final section addresses the modernisation process, detailing both the achievements and shortcomings of the negotiations, while also exploring the role of public perception in derailing the EU’s coordinated approach. The chapter concludes by questioning whether the ECT remains fit for purpose in light of the global climate crisis and evolving models of international economic governance. It argues that the Treaty’s legacy, whether reformed or terminated, will continue to shape investment protection in the energy sector and inform broader debates on the role of international law in balancing investment stability with regulatory autonomy in the pursuit of sustainable development.

detail.abstract:
The Court of Justice of the European Union landmark ruling in Achmea has profoundly influenced discussions on investor-State dispute settlement within the EU, extending its impact to the broader realm of international investment law. This article offers a jurisprudential analysis of Achmea’s continuing influence, focusing on its role as a defense in the enforcement of arbitral awards, as evidenced in recent cases in front of national courts of the United Kingdom and the United States. The advent of the “Achmea defense” echoes the “Achmea objections” encountered during arbitration, prompting a reassessment of jurisdictional and consent-related issues.

The contribution underscores a trend of national courts showing increasing deference to domestic legal tenets over international law, with a particular inclination towards accepting the Achmea defense. It posits that should this shift in judicial reasoning gain traction in higher courts, it may lead to domestic legal frameworks superseding international obligations delineated by the ICSID Convention and the New York Convention.

Focusing on the UK and US jurisdictions, the paper reveals complex issues relating to enforcement, execution, and consent, highlighting the imperative for ongoing scrutiny and engagement with the judicial evolution in response to Achmea across various legal systems. The article advocates for a dynamic interaction with post-Achmea judicial narratives and calls upon the legal and scholarly communities to delve into the intricate challenges facing the finality and binding authority of international arbitration.

detail.abstract: A new type of decision networks is suggested and its operation is analyzed. The network nodes are represented by intelligent agents who can denote either some biological beings, like humans, or neurons of the brain, or the nodes of artificial intelligence. The specifics of the network are in the following: It is probabilistic in the sense that the choice, accomplished by each agent, is characterized by the related probability. It is dynamic, with the probabilities varying in time due to the exchange of information between the agents. It is affective, because the agents choose between alternatives by taking account of utility as well as of biases and emotions. In general, it is heterogeneous, being composed of the groups of agents with different properties, for instance having long-term memory and short-term memory. The network dynamics, caused by the information exchange, results in decision error decrease. The network operation is illustrated by the example starting with the Allais paradox, its resolution, and the decision error diminution in the process of decision dynamics with information exchange. Resorting to machine-learning techniques it is possible to regulate the behavior of the network agents forcing them to choose particular alternatives.

detail.abstract:
Background: CfDNA methylation has emerged as a promising non-invasive biomarker for cancer detection. Conventional analytical approaches that rely on regional average methylation levels or single-CpG methylation levels are often constrained by limited feature resolution and may fail to capture methylation patterns embedded within individual sequencing fragments. These limitations highlight the need for read-level analysis, which preserves read-specific methylation profiles, thereby retaining higher-resolution epigenetic information and enabling more accurate characterization of biological heterogeneity and disease-associated signals. Moreover, by using individual sequencing reads as the fundamental input units, read-level methylation features can better preserve combinatorial methylation information within local genomic regions. Such fragment-level features are particularly well suited for deep learning models, allowing them to learn and represent complex epigenetic patterns with greater accuracy.

Methods: We developed AlphaBERT, a transformer-based deep learning framework for read-level classification of cfDNA methylation. By operating at read-level resolution, AlphaBERT models the methylation states (alpha values) of individual sequencing reads and preserves the intrinsic heterogeneity of tumor-derived signals. The framework adopts a two-stage training strategy, consisting of large-scale self-supervised pre-training on unlabeled whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) reads to learn contextual epigenetic representations, followed by supervised fine-tuning on labeled prostate cancer (PCa) and normal cfDNA samples for disease-specific classification. In addition, we designed a modified masked language modeling (MLM) objective to emphasize CpG site dependencies during representation learning.

Results: Compared with conventional deep learning models, AlphaBERT achieved superior diagnostic performance, with accuracy exceeding 92% and an AUC above 0.96, and showed high sensitivity and consistent stability for prostate cancer detection. It also effectively identified tumor-derived reads in simulated cfDNA mixtures with low tumor DNA fractions and showed potential for predicting treatment response in mCRPC. To support practical application, we developed PccMA (https://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/PccMA/), a user-friendly web platform for AlphaBERT-based prostate cancer risk estimation and cfDNA mixture simulation.

Conclusions: Our study demonstrates that read-level modeling of cfDNA methylation can effectively exploit read-level epigenetic heterogeneity for precision oncology applications. By bridging high-resolution molecular profiling with non-invasive diagnostics, AlphaBERT enables accurate detection, risk stratification, and treatment monitoring in prostate cancer.

detail.abstract: The paper conducts a comprehensive academic analysis of whether the Indian federal model offers a viable governance framework for contemporary Sudan amidst its devastating civil war and state fragmentation. Drawing on detailed scenario analysis, fiscal federalism data, and comparative constitutional assessment (World Bank, 2010; World Bank, 2021; IPC, 2026; FEWS NET, 2026; WFP/FAO/UNICEF, 2026), the paper argues that while India's "concessionary federalism" provides valuable principles for managing diversity through asymmetric arrangements and constitutional protection of minority rights (Academia.edu, 2024; Academic analysis, 2026), Sudan's crisis presents fundamental challenges-including armed fragmentation, external patronage networks, and humanitarian collapse-that transcend constitutional design. The paper presents three governance scenarios (continued partition, negotiated federalism, and warlord fragmentation), analyzing their probability, fiscal implications, and humanitarian consequences. It concludes that any resolution must address three interconnected prerequisites: sequenced demobilization with enforceable constitutional guarantees, interruption of external sponsorship through regional diplomacy, and a calibrated asymmetrical federal arrangement with constitutionally protected fiscal mechanisms.

detail.abstract: Cyanidation remains the dominant commercial method for gold extraction, but its acute toxicity, controlled-chemical status, detoxification requirements, and lifecycle liabilities motivate the evaluation of alternative lixiviants. This paper presents a non-experimental comparative conceptual techno-economic assessment of conventional cyanidation, pure glycine-oxidant leaching, and glycine-assisted low-cyanide leaching under Philippine conditions. Peer-reviewed metallurgical studies, Philippine commercial disclosures, official economic statistics, and applicable environmental and occupational-safety requirements were collected, normalized, and evaluated within a common process boundary. Masbate was used as the principal Philippine commercial benchmark. Public evidence supports a cyanidation overallrecovery screening range of approximately 69-80%, with 74-76% as the preliminary base checkpoint. Among pure-glycine systems, glycine-permanganate provided the strongest room-temperature whole-ore evidence, reporting 85.1% laboratory extraction at 30% solids, pH 10.5, 1.5 kg/t glycine, and 3 kg/t potassium permanganate. Glycine-hydrogen peroxide remained technically promising but carried greater uncertainty regarding oxidant decomposition, pulp density, residence time, recycle, and scale-up. The assessment finds that cyanidation is likely to remain the preliminary economic benchmark for ordinary free-milling Philippine ore because of commercial maturity and established downstream recovery. Pure glycine may become competitive where reagent recycle is efficient, net glycine loss and oxidant consumption are low, heating is unnecessary, or cyanide logistics and compliance costs are unusually high. Glycine-assisted low cyanide may provide the most practical transition for copper-bearing ores, although it remains subject to cyanide-specific controls. The paper concludes that process preference is conditional on mineralogy, overall recovery, reagent consumption, technology maturity, and site-specific Philippine costs. Results are screening-level and are not a feasibility or investment recommendation.

detail.abstract: We study how climate policy risk is priced across the maturity structure of equity cash flows. Using textual analysis of European news articles, we construct indices of transition and physical climate risk and, drawing on recent advances in measuring the temporal dimension of text, classify climate news by the horizon it references. We combine these indices with prices of dividend futures and dividend swaps, which allow us to decompose stock price reactions to climate news into short- and long-term cash-flow components. Heightened transition-risk news lowers stock prices, and the decline is concentrated in long-maturity dividend claims. The evidence suggests that investors expect most firms to defer adaptation, leaving near-term earnings and payouts largely unchanged while bearing greater long-run exposure. Finally, firm-level sensitivities identify which companies the market perceives as adapting early — accepting short-term losses to invest in the transition — versus those most exposed to stranded-asset risk.

detail.abstract: We hypothesize that the complexity of selecting personnel in a way that jointly optimizes for talent and diversity impedes organizations from meeting their diversity goals. To formalize this, we prove that maximizing cohort diversity is computationally complex and incorporate this complexity into a selection model by adding computational costs. To test the model's predictions, we construct an algorithm to estimate the diversity-talent frontier, which we apply to data from 10 talent programs (i.e., job training programs, scholarships, job placement platforms, etc.). We find that, on average, programs could have chosen cohorts that were 10% (14%) more diverse (more talented) without reducing talent (diversity). Leveraging a real intervention and counterfactual simulations, we show that access to a frontier estimate results in the selection of substantially more diverse and more talented cohorts. We conclude by demonstrating how the frontier estimation procedure can be used to evaluate the efficacy of alternative screening approaches. This generally reveals that if these programs had only screened on traditional metrics like IQ and test scores, they would have significantly reduced diversity and overlooked many of the most talented applicants.

detail.abstract: Deep neural forecasters for financial time series are conventionally optimized to minimize statistical loss functions such as the Mean Squared Error (MSE), yet they frequently suffer severe performance degradation when their raw predictive outputs are translated into live trading decisions. The principal culprit is not model inaccuracy per se, but the mismatch between the loss surface being minimized and the cost-laden objective that actually governs realized profit: bid-ask spreads, slippage, broker commissions, and the compounding drag of excessive portfolio turnover. In this paper we introduce the Volatility-Gated Inference (VGI) mechanism, a model-agnostic post-hoc policy that dynamically abstains from trade execution whenever normalized local volatility exceeds a calibrated threshold tau. We evaluate the proposal on EUR/USD daily exchange data from January 2019 through August 2026, comprising 1,980 trading days partitioned chronologically into 1,584 training and 396 out-of-sample testing days. The baseline directional model achieves a test MSE of 2.00 x 10^-5, yet its corresponding unconstrained trading strategy yields a cumulative return of -1.46% and an annualized Sharpe ratio of -0.13, evidence of capital erosion driven by over-trading. By contrast, the volatility-gated strategy, parameterized by a per-trade friction of c = 0.0001 and a normalized volatility threshold of tau = 1.0 sigma, achieves a cumulative return of +3.46% and an annualized Sharpe ratio of +0.36, while simultaneously reducing trade switches from approximately 280 to 145. These results demonstrate that selectively abstaining from execution in volatile regimes can invert a negative-expectancy strategy into a profitable one without any modification to the underlying predictive model.

detail.abstract:
What forces are driving Sudan apart? This paper argues that Sudan's current civil war (2023-2026) will most likely end not with a military victory by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) or the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), but with a cascade of secessions beginning in Eastern Sudan. Drawing on secession cascade theory (Griffiths, 2021), demographic transition theory (Urdal, 2006), geoeconomic analysis, and the rentier state literature (Beblawi & Luciani, 1987), the paper demonstrates that Eastern Sudan already possesses the fiscal resources to sustain an independent state: $1.67-2.29 billion in annual revenues from port customs, oil transit fees, gold exports, and agriculture. 

Two external actors-Eritrea and the United Arab Emirates (UAE)-are likely to accelerate this secession. Once the East secedes, Darfur (led by the RSF), the Nuba Mountains (probably uniting with South Sudan), and the northern Nile rump state (a de facto Egyptian protectorate) will follow. This fragmentation would produce severe regional spillovers: 3-5 million additional refugees, Sahel-wide arms trafficking, jihadist safe havens in Jebel Marra, and heightened Egyptian-Ethiopian tensions over Nile waters. 

But fragmentation is not inevitable. The paper proposes the Shield State (Dawlat al-Dir'i / ‫الدولة‬ ‫الدرعية‬) development model: a framework built on strategic self-sufficiency, raw material export bans, knowledge sovereignty, conditional foreign direct investment, economic security law, gender-inclusive industrialization, and green industrial policy. Comparative evidence from Ethiopia, Rwanda, and Bangladesh shows that such structural transformation is possible even under extreme fragility. The paper concludes with actionable policy recommendations for Sudanese and international actors and addresses counterarguments regarding WTO compliance, revenue transition costs, and state capacity.

detail.abstract:
Background: Long-term survival after lung transplantation remains heterogeneous. Conventional prognostic models may not adequately capture complex and nonlinear relationships among clinical factors. We aimed to develop, compare, and explain machine learning survival models for long-term survival prediction and risk stratification after lung transplantation.

Methods: We retrospectively analyzed adult primary lung transplant recipients in the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) registry from 1998 to 2024. A total of 17,519 recipients were randomly divided into training (n = 12,258) and independent hold-out validation (n = 5,261) cohorts. Five survival models were developed and compared. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, prediction error, and clinical utility. The best-performing model was further evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis and prognostic risk stratification.

Findings: Among 17,519 recipients, mean (standard deviation (SD)) age was 59 years (12), 10,481 (60%) were male, and mean (SD) follow-up was 6.8 years (2.9). XGBoost achieved the highest C-index (0.850), compared with 0.806 for random survival forest, 0.832 for gradient boosting machine, 0.767 for Cox proportional hazards, and 0.655 for neural network models. The XGBoost model achieved time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.900, 0.878, and 0.882 at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. SHAP analysis identified primary graft dysfunction status, hospitalization for infection, and bronchial stricture as the most influential predictors. Model performance remained favorable across predefined clinical subgroups. Model-derived risk scores significantly separated recipients into different groups with distinct long-term survival trajectories (log-rank p < 0.001).

Interpretation: An explainable XGBoost survival model demonstrated strong discrimination and clinically meaningful risk stratification after lung transplantation. The findings highlight primary graft dysfunction, infection-related hospitalization, and bronchial stricture as important contributors to long-term prognosis. The model may provide a framework for postoperative prognostic stratification, although temporal and external validation and prospective evaluation are needed before clinical implementation.

title: A frequency-dynamic attention modulation architecture for atrial fibrillation detection

detail.title: A frequency-dynamic attention modulation architecture for atrial fibrillation detection
detail.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most prevalent and serious cardiac arrhythmias, yet its episodic and asymptomatic nature renders it difficult to detect using electrocardiography (ECG), necessitating robust automated diagnostic systems for timely intervention. However, the existing strategies particularly those built on self-attention mechanisms inherently operate as low-pass filters, progressively attenuating high-frequency morphological details across layers and giving rise to the frequency vanishing problem. To this end, we propose ECG Frequency-Dynamic Attention Modulation (ECG-FDAM), a novel framework that endows transformer-based ECG classifiers with input-adaptive, full-spectrum frequency control. Our mechanism integrates two synergistic modules Attention Inversion (AttInv), which synthesises a complementary high-pass pathway alleviating frequency vanishing and Frequency Dynamic Scaling (FreqScale), which adaptively reweights three clinically bands to enhance diagnostically relevant components. The results across two public databases demonstrate that ECG-FDAM consistently outperforms several baselines with an accuracy of 99.0\%. Ablation studies confirm the indispensable contribution of each module, while theoretical analyses guarantee stable gradient flow and spectral preservation and visualisations reveal that the model attends to clinically plausible morphological signatures. ECG-FDAM provides a principled, scalable and interpretable solution for automated AF detection, with the potential for integration into clinical workflows and wearable monitoring systems to facilitate arrhythmia screening.

detail.abstract:
Background: U.S. opioid overdose mortality declined after 2023 even as fentanyl remained dominant in unregulated markets. We modeled the displacement of heroin by illicitly manufactured fentanyl as a market diffusion process and examined whether fentanyl’s association with mortality changed across the market transition.

Methods: We fit state-specific logistic curves to fentanyl and heroin reports from the U.S. National Forensic Laboratory Information System to characterize the heroin-to-fentanyl market transition across 50 states and the District of Columbia from 2015-2025. We then conducted two-way fixed-effects panel analyses of opioid overdose mortality in 45 states using mortality data from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The primary quadratic model assessed whether the fentanyl-mortality association attenuated as market penetration increased.

Findings: Fentanyl’s displacement of heroin followed strongly logistic trajectories (median R2=0·98). State diffusion midpoints ranged from 2015-2022; later-transitioning states transitioned more rapidly than early-transitioning states (mean 1·7 vs 3·1 years). As fentanyl displaced heroin, further increases in fentanyl market share were associated with progressively less additional mortality: A 10-percentage-point increase in fentanyl market share was associated with long-run mortality increases of 20.9% at 25% market share, 11.5% at 50% market share, and 2.8% at 75% market share. The fentanyl-associated mortality component stabilized after 2022 as observed mortality declined.

Interpretation: Fentanyl’s mortality association was phase-dependent: additional market penetration was most strongly associated with mortality during active heroin displacement and attenuated as markets approached saturation. The mortality decline after 2022 is consistent with the heroin-to-fentanyl transition having largely run its course.

detail.abstract: Risk normalization standardizes gross payoff geometry, not necessarily the scaling laws of implementation costs or eligibility. We derive the necessary and sufficient cost transformation for invariance conditional on a fixed gross risk-unit path. For a constant per-contract dollar cost component and point value, average normalized drag is governed by harmonic risk width. When drag is lower in a late period, downscaling can lower benchmark net performance in both periods while enlarging their measured contrast. detail.abstract:
The development of exchange rate theories takes the Mundell-Fleming model as a dividing point. Before this, balance of payments theories focused on the balance of the current account and completely ignored the capital and financial account. After this, exchange rate determination theories established the dominant position of the capital and financial account and tried to explain exchange rate changes through price signals such as interest rates, inflation, and income levels. The author believes that price signals are essentially results of economic operation, while the competitive advantages of a country's goods, services, and assets in the international market are the fundamental reasons that determine exchange rate changes.

This paper attempts to move away from the theoretical framework of exchange rate determination theories, adjust the balance of payments identity, and weaken the distinction between the current account and the capital and financial account. It establishes the core role of the exchange rate in balancing the balance of payments in the identity, and completes a closed loop of 1. local changes cause imbalance of the identity → 2. imbalance of the identity causes exchange rate changes → 3. exchange rate changes affect overall changes → 4. overall changes offset local changes. It also expresses the rate of exchange rate change as the ratio of the imbalance rate of the balance of payments identity to exchange rate elasticity.

Finally, by analyzing the fundamental and non-fundamental factors of the competitive advantages of Chinese and American goods, services, and assets in the international market, the long-term trend of the RMB against the US dollar exchange rate is judged.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the technical feasibility of replacing human-mediated administrative processes across the European Union with specialised large language models and agentic systems operating under European jurisdiction. Once continuous high-assurance identity recognition is solved, the generation and issuance of official identifiers-company registrations, VAT numbers, professional licences, permits, residency documents, and related credentials-becomes a pure information-processing task. Properly constrained and specialised models, continuously grounded in authoritative registries and statutory text, can achieve higher consistency and closer fidelity to written rules than unconstrained human caseworkers on well-specified rule-application tasks. The binding constraints are architectural specialisation, data interlinkage, provenance, and residual constitutional oversight-not raw model capability or absolute compute scarcity. I specify a scientific method for proving feasibility: formal task decomposition, controlled administrative benchmarks prioritising fidelity to enacted law, compute budgeting via FLOPs and measured throughput, narrow-domain pilots with quantitative latency and error metrics, and stress-testing of hybrid appellate layers under realistic volumes. Using publicly available 2026 data on EuroHPC systems, AI Factories, and the emerging AI Gigafactory programme, I show that existing and near-term European classical compute is already sufficient for training specialised administrative model families via knowledge distillation and for sustaining high-volume inference. Quantum resources remain NISQ-scale and are relevant only for hybrid optimisation subroutines. The technology is feasible; the decisive variables are institutional design, data quality, and engineered residual human accountability.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how the Russia-Ukraine war transmitted to household nutrition and welfare in low and middle-income countries through two simultaneous channels: a fertilizer input-cost shock that raised staple food prices, and a broader commodity price shock that crowded out non-food household expenditure. Existing literature typically treats these as separate shocks. This paper models them as a joint household budget squeeze using a dynamic Stone-Geary household optimization framework with a countryvarying borrowing constraint, and evaluates the mechanism against real, directly measured fertilizer and metals price data from the World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook, fertilizer trade-dependence data from UN Comtrade, and food and non-food consumer price divergence for Nigeria and Malawi. The fertilizer shock measured directly from the data peaked at 193 percent above its pre-shock baseline in April 2022 and was both larger and more persistent than the accompanying metals shock. Nigeria and Malawi are shown to sit at opposite extremes of direct Russia and Belarus fertilizer dependence, with Nigeria’s exposure concentrated almost entirely in potassium chloride imports. A calibrated simulation of the household model, run on the real shock series, finds that both countries’ financial buffers were exhausted well before the shock peaked, and that Malawi’s borrowing constraint bound for more months than Nigeria’s despite far lower direct supplier-country exposure, consistent with the paper’s central claim that global price transmission and financial buffer capacity jointly determine welfare loss independent of direct trade exposure. The paper reports this as a working result: a known limitation in the current consumption-allocation rule used in the simulation is identified and a methodological correction is specified before the point estimates can be treated as final.

detail.abstract: Trading firms routinely pay departing employees to sit out of the market for six months to two years under garden leave and noncompete arrangements, at a privately contracted rate ranging from base salary-the customary minimum, commonly $150,000-$200,000 per year-up to full compensation. This proposal asks what that money buys. Two motives are observationally similar but carry opposite welfare implications: firms may be protecting proprietary knowledge until it depreciates, an appropriability mechanism that sustains innovation incentives; or they may be paying to deny rivals access to scarce talent itself, a form of upstream foreclosure that misallocates human capital. I develop a contract-design model in which a departing worker carries two assets-firm-specific knowledge that decays at a strategy-specific rate and general ability that does not-and show that the two motives leave distinct fingerprints on observable contract features. The motive is identified not from exclusion length alone but from how contract design responds to knowledge half-life, rival demand, and destination: protection predicts sitout lengths that track knowledge half-lives; blocking predicts lengths pinned at legal maxima, insensitive to knowledge decay, escalating with rival entry, and targeted at competitor-bound moves. The financial trading industry is the unique setting in which these design features are observable: regulatory personnel registers measure realized sit-outs and destinations at the person level, alpha-decay rates vary sharply and measurably across strategy classes, and the price of exclusion-heterogeneous across firms and workers, and only partially disclosedis bounded below by posted base salaries and observed in structure through litigation and disclosure records, with its heterogeneity itself supplying an additional testable prediction. The empirical design combines register-based gap panels, entity-level strategy classification, fundentry threat measures, and policy events in the UK, New York, and California to separate the two mechanisms and to inform the contested regulation of noncompete agreements.

detail.title: Self-Fulfilling Forecasts in a Minimal LLM Market: An Experimental Test of Performative Feedback Strength
